newsitem.title: USA: Dead heat in Mass. Senate race - poll.
newsitem.headline: Dead heat in Mass. Senate race - poll.

text.p: Democratic Sen. John Kerry and Republican Gov. William Weld, competing in one of the most closely watched Senate races in the nation, are locked in a virtual dead heat, a poll showed Friday.

With two weeks to go before the election, Kerry, seeking his third six-year term, led Weld 44 percent to 40 percent, within the poll's five percentage point margin of error, the Boston Herald reported.

Twelve percent of the 403 likely voters polled Wednesday and Thursday said they remain undecided and 4 percent said they support a third candidate. A Herald poll released last week showed Kerry with a lead of 46 percent to 40 percent.
With Weld hitting hard at Kerry's use of cut-rate housing from two developers and a lobbyist in the 1980s, the Herald said both candidates' favourable ratings have dropped over the last week.

"As the campaign has turned decidedly negative it's turning voters off," said pollster Kelly Myers, director of the University of New Hampshire Survey Centre, who conducted the survey. "The attacks have driven Kerry's negatives up but it's come at a cost to Weld's campaign."
Kerry's favourable to unfavourable rating dropped to 50-38 percent from 55-33 percent last week but Weld's slipped further, to 54-36 percent from 61-28 percent.

Weld also accused Kerry of violating an agreement to a campaign spending limit, charging that the senator contributed nearly $1 million to his campaign. Kerry shot back, slamming Weld for taking money from political action committees. As of Oct. 16, the Weld campaign had $666,000 in the bank, more than double Kerry's $289,000, according to news reports.
